cases.title: The main risk summary rendered JavaScript objects
cases.reproduction: A v3 report with risk-domain state totals rendered [object Object] in Markdown and HTML.
cases.impact: The first human-readable summary was damaged even though the structured JSON remained available.
cases.repair: Render byState[state].total and bySeverity explicitly and omit zero-count states.
cases.plantedFailure: Restoring the v0.5.1 renderer must make the golden Markdown and HTML assertions fail.
cases.remainingBoundary: Golden rendering tests protect the current fixture shapes; they do not prove every future presentation is understandable.

cases.title: A pnpm workspace could receive a false confirmed lockfile absence
cases.reproduction: A root pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml covering apps/* still allowed a child package.json to be reported as confirmed missing-lockfile evidence.
cases.impact: The strongest evidence state was assigned without actually resolving the applicable workspace boundary.
cases.repair: Parse bounded pnpm workspace includes and exclusions; malformed or unsupported metadata becomes incomplete evidence and unknown instead of confirmed absence.
cases.plantedFailure: Restoring the adjacent-lockfile-only decision must make the covered pnpm workspace fixture fail.
cases.remainingBoundary: The parser supports the documented bounded subset and is not a general YAML evaluator.

cases.title: Nested JS/TS templates could make a whole file partial
cases.reproduction: A nested template such as const html = `${``}` produced unterminated_string_literal and stopped normal source-rule coverage for that file.
cases.impact: The tool failed closed as unknown, but relevant server-rendered code was left unexamined until the user noticed the coverage warning.
cases.repair: Track nested template and expression depth while continuing to inspect executable expressions, including TSX braces.
cases.plantedFailure: Restoring the v0.5.1 tokenizer must make the nested-template coverage fixture fail.
cases.remainingBoundary: The tokenizer is still bounded and reports unsupported syntax as incomplete evidence rather than silently passing it.

cases.title: A path-only rename could make a retest exit successfully
cases.reproduction: Renaming a file without removing its condition produced one fixed and one new finding, allowing the compatible baseline gate to exit successfully.
cases.impact: The condition still existed, while the baseline presentation implied that the old condition had been fixed.
cases.repair: Pair only one-to-one path-independent equivalents and keep them unchanged with condition_moved; ambiguous duplicates remain unmatched.
cases.plantedFailure: Restoring path-bound-only matching must make the rename retest assertion fail.
cases.remainingBoundary: condition_moved means an equivalent condition exists elsewhere; it does not prove historical identity or that a git move caused it.
